title: What Physical AI and scientific machine learning are
summary: Scientific machine learning blends physical laws with learning from data. Physical AI puts such models into machines that sense and act in the real world, from robots to automated vehicles.
outcomes: say what scientific machine learning (SciML) and Physical AI mean, in one sentence each
place a model on the spectrum from physics-based to data-driven
explain why pure data fits fail outside the data and pure physics misses details
name three transport problems where SciML helps
narration_en: Engineers have always had two ways to predict the world. The first is physics: write down the laws, such as conservation of mass or Newton's laws, and solve them. The second is data: collect measurements and fit a pattern. Physics models extrapolate well but miss details we did not model. Data models capture details but fail where they have no data. Scientific machine learning, or SciML, combines the two. It builds machine learning models that respect physical laws, discovers equations from data, and builds fast surrogates of slow simulations. Physical AI goes one step further: it puts such models inside machines that sense and act in the physical world, such as robots, drones and automated vehicles, where mistakes have physical consequences. In transport, SciML estimates traffic from a few sensors, predicts crash risk, emulates climate and energy models, and runs digital twins of cities. In this module you will slide a model from pure data to pure physics and see where each one breaks.
narration_ar: لدى المهندسين منذ القدم طريقتان للتنبؤ بالعالم. الأولى هي الفيزياء: نكتب القوانين، مثل حفظ الكتلة أو قوانين نيوتن، ثم نحلها. والثانية هي البيانات: نجمع القياسات ونستخرج نمطاً منها. تستقرئ النماذج الفيزيائية جيداً لكنها تغفل تفاصيل لم ننمذجها، أما نماذج البيانات فتلتقط التفاصيل لكنها تخفق حيث لا توجد بيانات. ويجمع تعلم الآلة العلمي بين الطريقتين: فهو يبني نماذج تعلم آلي تحترم القوانين الفيزيائية، ويكتشف المعادلات من البيانات، ويبني بدائل سريعة لمحاكاة بطيئة. ويذهب الذكاء الاصطناعي المادي خطوة أبعد، إذ يضع هذه النماذج داخل آلات تستشعر العالم المادي وتتصرف فيه، كالروبوتات والطائرات المسيّرة والمركبات الآلية، حيث تكون للأخطاء عواقب مادية. وفي النقل يقدّر تعلم الآلة العلمي حركة المرور من عدد قليل من أجهزة الاستشعار، ويتنبأ بخطر الحوادث، ويحاكي نماذج المناخ والطاقة، ويشغّل توائم رقمية للمدن. ستحرك في هذه الوحدة نموذجاً من البيانات الخالصة إلى الفيزياء الخالصة وترى أين يخفق كل منهما.

diagram.title: Two ways of knowing, and the bridge between them
diagram.caption: Physics gives structure, data gives detail; scientific machine learning combines them, and Physical AI acts on the result.

nodes.label: Physical laws
nodes.detail: Equations we trust: conservation of mass and energy, Newton's laws, traffic-flow and heat equations. They hold everywhere, even where we have no data.

nodes.label: Data
nodes.detail: Measurements from sensors, cameras, simulations and experiments. Rich in detail, but noisy, incomplete and only where we looked.

nodes.label: Scientific ML
nodes.detail: Machine learning that respects physics: physics-informed networks, equation discovery, operator learning, hybrid models and surrogates.

nodes.label: Trustworthy model
nodes.detail: A model that fits the data, obeys the laws, extrapolates sensibly and can run fast enough to use.

nodes.label: Physical AI
nodes.detail: Robots, drones, automated vehicles and smart infrastructure that use such models to act in the real world, safely.

nodes.label: Uncertainty
nodes.detail: Every model is wrong somewhere. Knowing how wrong, and where, is what makes a model safe to use for decisions.

tour.text: Physics: laws that hold everywhere, but only describe what we chose to model.
Data: rich detail, but only where and when we measured.
Scientific machine learning uses both: physics for structure, data for detail.
The goal is a model that is accurate, general and fast.
Physical AI puts such models inside machines that sense and act.
And every model must say how sure it is.

sections.heading: Two ways to predict
sections.html: Physics-based models start from laws: mass is conserved, force equals mass times acceleration, heat flows from hot to cold. They work even in situations never measured, but only describe what we put in. Data-driven models learn patterns from examples. They capture details nobody wrote down, but they can be badly wrong outside the range of their data.

sections.heading: Scientific machine learning
sections.html:
Scientific machine learning (SciML) combines the two. Its main tools, which you will meet in this course:

  • Physics-informed neural networks: networks trained to fit data and obey an equation.
  • Equation discovery: finding the law itself from data.
  • Operator learning and surrogates: fast stand-ins for slow simulators.
  • Hybrid models: physics plus a learned correction.
  • Uncertainty quantification: saying how sure we are.

sections.heading: Physical AI
sections.html: Physical AI is artificial intelligence that perceives and acts in the physical world: robots, drones, automated vehicles, smart traffic signals. Its models must respect physics (a car cannot stop instantly), run in real time and be safe when wrong. That is why SciML and Physical AI belong together: physical structure makes learned models more reliable.

sections.heading: Why transport needs it
sections.html: Transport is full of physics (traffic waves, vehicle dynamics, energy) and full of data (detectors, cameras, phones), but data are always sparse where it matters: during crashes, at extreme densities, in future climates. Go 3 applies SciML to traffic estimation, automated vehicles, safety, energy and emissions, integrated assessment models such as GCAM, crowds and digital twins.

callouts.title: Research angle
callouts.html: Many transport problems are 'small data' problems in disguise: plenty of normal data, very little about the rare events we care about. Physics is how we bridge that gap.

explorer.predict: Which model will predict best after t = 2: the data fit, the physics model, or a mix?

code.title: Data fit versus physics
code.source:
import numpy as np
rng = np.random.default_rng(11)
truth = lambda t: np.exp(-0.3*t)*np.cos(2*t)
phys = lambda t: np.exp(-0.45*t)*np.cos(1.85*t)   # physics model, slightly wrong parameters
t_data = np.linspace(0, 2, 8)
y_data = truth(t_data) + 0.05*rng.standard_normal(8)
coef = np.polyfit(t_data, y_data, 5)              # pure data model
t_new = np.linspace(2.1, 6, 40)
err = lambda f: np.sqrt(np.mean((f(t_new) - truth(t_new))**2))
print(f'data fit error beyond the data: {err(lambda t: np.polyval(coef, t)):.2f}')
print(f'physics error beyond the data:  {err(phys):.2f}')
code.explain: A degree-5 polynomial fits 8 points well but explodes after t = 2; the slightly wrong physics model stays close.
code.expected:
data fit error beyond the data: 259.02
physics error beyond the data:  0.13

takeaways: Physics extrapolates but misses details; data captures details but fails outside its range.
Scientific machine learning combines physical laws with learning from data.
Physical AI puts models into machines that sense and act in the real world.
Transport is physics-rich but data-sparse where it matters most.

AI systems that perceive and act in the physical world, such as robots and automated vehicles.
A model learned from examples without built-in laws.
